status: Experimental transport foundation; not yet connected to the application UI or shipped as working Bluetooth sync.

platforms.Windows: Windowless native RFCOMM connector; requests authenticated and encrypted Bluetooth link; no drivers or console helper. Built locally with static C++ runtime; pure address/service self-test passes.
platforms.macOS: Transient RFCOMM service, accepts OS-paired peers only; permission usage text embedded. Compile verification is pending CI. Actual listen/connect is never run by CI self-tests.

relay: A bounded, credit-controlled multiplexer carries both devices' normal application connections across one byte stream. Local listeners bind only 127.0.0.1; remote opens can target only the configured local CrossPaste port. No arbitrary destination proxy.
trust: The transport handshake only checks framing/version/role. Existing CrossPaste pairing and authenticated/encrypted requests must remain above it. Native Bluetooth pairing/permissions are not automated.
tests: Three framing checks and three real-loopback integration checks pass on Windows, including 12 simultaneous bidirectional requests larger than the credit window, half-close handling, disconnect cleanup, and same-role rejection. These do not prove a real Bluetooth link.
remaining: macOS native compilation and runtime verification
application endpoint routing and device UI integration
